physical_harm: Severe bullet injuries leading to death
premeditation_planning: Yes, the court found premeditation and planning to attack the deceased
motive: Grudge against the deceased for standing against the students' movement
key_evidence_accepted: The statement of approver (PW-6) was confidence inspiring and stood corroborated by the medical evidence of PW-14 and the post mortem examination report (Ex. 7). The analysis of statement of various persons, particularly eye-witnesses clearly strengthen the case of PW-6, approver, in all aspects including conspiracy, planning to attack the deceased, actual incident, role played by the assailants and subsequent events after the gunshot till the death of the deceased.
witness_credibility: The evidence of hostile witness can be relied upon at least up to the extent he supported the case of prosecution. The evidence of eye witnesses including the hostile witnesses, firmly established the prosecution version. Five eye-witnesses clearly identified two convicts-appellants, and other accused persons were identified by more than one eye-witnesses. The ocular evidence of the approver (PW-6) stood corroborated by the medical evidence of PW-14 and the post mortem examination report (Ex. 7).
post_offence_conduct: PW-6 asserted that he had decided to disclose the whole incident voluntarily on the advise of the members of his family. He identified all the accused persons in the Court by name and face. He also denied that he deposed falsely and denied that he was provoked that if he turns to be an approver, he would be given a suitable job.
custody_duration: PW-6 was in police custody for eight days
bail_history: PW-6 was granted bail after expiry of police remand
trial_duration: Trial commenced on 11.03.2003; judgment delivered on 19.04.2005; appeals heard in High Court and Supreme Court
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused and the State in the Supreme Court not specified in the judgment text
appeal_history: Trial court acquitted ten accused and convicted two; High Court set aside acquittal of four and convicted them; Supreme Court confirmed High Court's decision
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused persons developed a grudge against 'T' for opposing the students' movement and planned to eliminate him. The approver's (PW-6) statement, corroborated by eye-witnesses and medical evidence, established the common intention and planning of the attack, leading to the conviction of six accused persons under Section 302/34 IPC.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the trial court's acquittal of ten accused persons was justified, and the High Court's reversal of those acquittals was unwarranted. They contended that the approver's (PW-6) statement was uncorroborated and that the trial court's findings should not be disturbed without compelling reasons.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that common intention among participants in a crime is essential for invoking Section 34 IPC, and that corroboration is necessary for the testimony of an accomplice unless the evidence is trustworthy and supported by other evidence.

sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed based on the conviction of the accused under Section 302 IPC for murder, with life imprisonment as the punishment, supported by the evidence of the approver and eye-witnesses establishing the common intention and planning of the crime.
